questions.question: When an article is sold at its marked price, it gives a profit of 25% If a discount of 9.6% is allowed on the marked price, then the profit percent will be:
questions.questionHtml: When an article is sold at its marked price, it gives a profit of 25% If a discount of 9.6% is allowed on the marked price, then the profit percent will be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100.

Profit = 25% when sold at MP → Marked Price (MP) = 125.

New Selling Price (SP) after 9.6% discount = 125 × (100 − 9.6)% = 125 × 90.4%.

New SP = 1.25 × 90.4 = 113.

Profit % = New SP − CP = 113 − 100 = 13%.

∴ The correct answer is 13%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Profit at Marked Price = 25%

Discount offered on Marked Price = 9.6%

Formula Used:

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

SP = MP − Discount

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100.

⇒ Since selling at MP gives 25% profit, MP = 100 + 25% of 100 = 125.

⇒ Discount amount = 9.6% of MP = (9.6 ÷ 100) × 125.

⇒ Discount amount = (9.6 × 1.25) = 12.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 125 − 12 = 113.

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 113 − 100 = 13.

⇒ Profit % = (13 ÷ 100) × 100 = 13%.

∴ The correct answer is 13%.

Additional Information

Relationship between CP and MP

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is given by CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are allowed, the equivalent single discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Effective Profit Percentage

Effective Profit % = Mark up % − Discount % − (Mark up % × Discount % ÷ 100).

questions.question: The bisector of ∠B in ΔABC meets AC at D. If AB = 10 cm, BC = 11 cm and AC = 14 cm, then the length of AD is∶
questions.questionHtml: The bisector of ∠B in ΔABC meets AC at D. If AB = 10 cm, BC = 11 cm and AC = 14 cm, then the length of AD is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

According to the Angle Bisector Theorem, the ratio AD : DC is equal to the ratio AB : BC.

Ratio AD : DC = 10 : 11

Total parts in AC = 10 + 11 = 21 units

Value of 21 units = 14 cm

Value of 10 units (AD) = (14 ÷ 21) × 10 = (2/3) × 10 = 20/3 cm

∴ The correct answer is 20/3 cm.

Alternate Method

Given: AB = 10 cm, BC = 11 cm, AC = 14 cm.

In ΔABC, BD is the internal bisector of ∠B.

Formula Used: Angle Bisector Theorem states AD/DC = AB/BC.

⇒ Let AD = x cm, then DC = (14 − x) cm.

⇒ AD / DC = AB / BC

⇒ x / (14 − x) = 10 / 11

⇒ 11x = 10 × (14 − x)

⇒ 11x = 140 − 10x

⇒ 11x + 10x = 140

⇒ 21x = 140

⇒ x = 140 / 21

⇒ x = 20 / 3

∴ The correct answer is 20/3 cm.

Additional Information

Length of Internal Angle Bisector

The length of the angle bisector BD can be calculated using the formula: BD2 = AB × BC − AD × DC.

External Angle Bisector Theorem

If the bisector of an external angle of a triangle intersects the extended opposite side at a point D', then AD' / CD' = AB / BC.

Incenter Property

The internal angle bisectors of a triangle are concurrent at a point called the incenter, which is equidistant from all sides.

questions.question: If the curved surface area of a solid cylinder is one-third of its total surface area, then what is the ratio of its diameter to its height?
questions.questionHtml: If the curved surface area of a solid cylinder is one-third of its total surface area, then what is the ratio of its diameter to its height?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Curved surface area of cylinder = 2 πrh

Total surface area of cylinder = 2 πr(h + r)

According to the question

[2 πrh/2 πr (r + h)] = 1/3

⇒ 3h = h + r

⇒ 3h – h = r

⇒ 2h = r

⇒ h/r = 1/2

⇒ h/2r = 1/4

⇒ 4/1 = 2r/h

So, ratio of diameter to height of cylinder = 4 : 1

questions.question: The ratio of the incomes of A and B last year was 4 ∶ 3, respectively. The ratios of their individual incomes of the last year and the present year are 3 ∶ 4 and 5 ∶ 6, respectively. If their total income for the present year is Rs. 8.04 lakh, then the income of B last year was∶
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the incomes of A and B last year was 4 ∶ 3, respectively. The ratios of their individual incomes of the last year and the present year are 3 ∶ 4 and 5 ∶ 6, respectively. If their total income for the present year is Rs. 8.04 lakh, then the income of B last year was∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio A : B (Last Year) = 4 : 3

A (Present) = 4 × (4 ÷ 3) = 16/3 | B (Present) = 3 × (6 ÷ 5) = 18/5

Ratio A : B (Present) = (16/3) : (18/5) = 80 : 54 = 40 : 27

Total units = 40 + 27 = 67 units → Rs. 8.04 lakh

1 unit = 0.12 lakh ⇒ B Last Year = (5 ÷ 6) × (27 × 0.12) = 2.7 lakh

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2.7 lakh.

Alternate Method

Given:

Ratio of incomes of A and B (Last Year) = 4 : 3

Individual ratio A (Last : Present) = 3 : 4

Individual ratio B (Last : Present) = 5 : 6

Total Present Income = Rs. 8.04 lakh

Calculations:

⇒ Let last year incomes be AL = 4x and BL = 3x.

⇒ APresent = AL × (4 ÷ 3) = 4x × 4/3 = 16x/3

⇒ BPresent = BL × (6 ÷ 5) = 3x × 6/5 = 18x/5

⇒ Total Present Income = 16x/3 + 18x/5 = 8.04

⇒ (80x + 54x) ÷ 15 = 8.04

⇒ 134x ÷ 15 = 8.04

⇒ 134x = 8.04 × 15 = 120.6

⇒ x = 120.6 ÷ 134 = 0.9

⇒ Income of B last year = 3x = 3 × 0.9 = 2.7 lakh

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2.7 lakh.

Additional Information

Compounded Ratio

For two or more ratios, the compounded ratio is the ratio of the product of the antecedents to the product of the consequents (e.g., for a:b and c:d, it is ac:bd).

Inverse Ratio

The inverse ratio of a:b is b:a. It is often used in speed-time and work-efficiency problems.

Continued Proportion

Three quantities a, b, and c are in continued proportion if a:b = b:c, where b is the mean proportional (b2 = ac).

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 90 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
questions.questionHtml: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the current is 6 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 90 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Downstream Speed (v + u) = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h

Upstream Speed (v − u) = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h

Total Time = (Distance ÷ Downstream Speed) + (Distance ÷ Upstream Speed)

Total Time = (90 ÷ 24) + (90 ÷ 12) = 3.75 + 7.5 = 11.25 hours

∴ The correct answer is 11¼ hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of boat (B) = 18 km/h

Speed of current (C) = 6 km/h

Distance (D) = 90 km

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Downstream Speed = Speed of boat + Speed of current

Upstream Speed = Speed of boat − Speed of current

Calculations:

⇒ Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h

⇒ Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h

⇒ Time for downstream trip = 90 ÷ 24 = 3.75 hours

⇒ Time for upstream trip = 90 ÷ 12 = 7.5 hours

⇒ Total time = 3.75 + 7.5 = 11.25 hours

⇒ 11.25 hours = 11 + 0.25 = 11 + (1/4) = 11¼ hours

∴ The correct answer is 11¼ hours.

Additional Information

Speed in Still Water

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are known, Speed of boat = (D + U) ÷ 2.

Speed of Current

If downstream speed (D) and upstream speed (U) are known, Speed of current = (D − U) ÷ 2.

Average Speed for Round Trip

Average Speed = (Downstream Speed × Upstream Speed) ÷ Still Water Speed = (D × U) ÷ B.

questions.question: A person sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 33 more, he would have gained 14%. To gain 25%, he should sell the article for∶
questions.questionHtml: A person sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 33 more, he would have gained 14%. To gain 25%, he should sell the article for∶
questions.solution:
Let the CP of the article be Rs. x

If article sold at 16% below its cost price, then SP of the article = x × (84/100) = 0.84x

If article sold at 14% above its cost price, then SP of the article = x × (114/100) = 1.14x

According to the question

⇒ 1.14x – 0.84x = 33

⇒ 0.3x = 33

⇒ x = 33/0.3

⇒ x = 110

To gain 25% on CP, then SP of the article = 110 × (125/100) = 137.5

Short Trick∶

Let CP of the article be 100%, it should be sold at 125% to gain 25%

⇒ 16% + 14% = 33

⇒ 30% = 33

⇒ 125% = (33/30) × 125 = 137.5

questions.question: The average weight of a certain number of students in a group is 72 kg. If 10 students having an average weight of 78kg leave and 4 students having an average weight of 80 kg join the group, the average weight of the students in the group decreases by 0.7 kg. The number of students initially in the group is:
questions.questionHtml: The average weight of a certain number of students in a group is 72 kg. If 10 students having an average weight of 78kg leave and 4 students having an average weight of 80 kg join the group, the average weight of the students in the group decreases by 0.7 kg. The number of students initially in the group is:
questions.solution:
Average weight of some students be = 72 kg

Deviation of weight of 10 students who leave the class = (78 – 72) × 10 = 60 kg

Deviation of weigh of 4 students who join the class = (80 – 72) × 4 = 32 kg

Let the number of students after be x then,

⇒ 0.7 × x = 60 – 32

⇒ x = 28/0.7 = 40

∴ Number of students was initially = 40 + 10 – 4 = 46

questions.question: In a class, \(83\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. If 60% of the number of boys and 80% of the number of girls are present, then what percentage of the total number of students in the class is absent?
questions.questionHtml: In a class, \(83\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the number of students are girls and the rest are boys. If 60% of the number of boys and 80% of the number of girls are present, then what percentage of the total number of students in the class is absent?
questions.solution:
Let total number of students in class be x

Number of girls = x × (5/6) = 5x/6

Number of boys = x × (1/6) = x/6

Number of absent girls = (5x/6) × (20/100) = x/6

Number of absent boys = (x/6) × (40/100) = x/15

Total number of students who absent = (x/6) + (x/15) = (5x + 2x)/30 = 7x/30

Percentage of students who absent = [(7x/30)/x] × 100 = 70/3% = \(23\frac{1}{3}\)

questions.question: A sum lent out at simple interest amounts to Rs. 6076 in 1 year and Rs. 7504 in 3 years. The sum and the rate of interest (approx) p.a are respectively:
questions.questionHtml: A sum lent out at simple interest amounts to Rs. 6076 in 1 year and Rs. 7504 in 3 years. The sum and the rate of interest (approx) p.a are respectively:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 2 years (3 yr − 1 yr) = 7504 − 6076 = Rs. 1428

Interest for 1 year = 1428 ÷ 2 = Rs. 714

Principal (Sum) = Amount (1 yr) − Interest (1 yr) = 6076 − 714 = Rs. 5362

Rate % = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100 = (714 ÷ 5362) × 100 ≈ 13.32%

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5,362 and 13.32%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 1 year (A1) = Rs. 6076

Amount after 3 years (A3) = Rs. 7504

Formula Used:

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal × Rate × Time ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 2 years (3 − 1 years) = A3 − A1

⇒ SI for 2 years = Rs. 7504 − Rs. 6076 = Rs. 1428

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1428 ÷ 2 = Rs. 714

⇒ Principal (Sum) = Amount after 1 year − SI for 1 year

⇒ Principal = 6076 − 714 = Rs. 5362

⇒ Rate of Interest (R) = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

⇒ R = (714 × 100) ÷ (5362 × 1)

⇒ R ≈ 13.3159% → 13.32%

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5,362 and 13.32%.

Additional Information

Nature of Simple Interest

In Simple Interest, the interest earned remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the initial principal (P).

Amount and Principal Relation

Amount after T years is A = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100. If we know the amounts at different years, the difference in amounts gives the interest for that specific time gap.

Effective Rate of Interest

For SI, the effective rate for T years is simply R × T. In Compound Interest, the effective rate is calculated using the formula [ (1 + R/100)T − 1 ] × 100.

questions.question: The value of 9 × 6 ÷ 24 + 8 ÷ 2 of 5 – 30 ÷ 4 of 4 + 27 × 5 ÷ 9 is∶

Given:

9 × 6 ÷ 24 + 8 ÷ 2 of 5 – 30 ÷ 4 of 4 + 27 × 5 ÷ 9 = ?

BODMAS Rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

Calculation:

⇒ 9 × 6 ÷ 24 + 8 ÷ 10 – 30 ÷ 16 + 27 × 5 ÷ 9

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: A circle is inscribed in quadrilateral ABCD touching AB, BC, CD and AD at the points P, Q, R and S, respectively, and ∠B = 90°. If AD = 24 cm, AB = 27 cm and DR = 6 cm, then what is the circumference of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: A circle is inscribed in quadrilateral ABCD touching AB, BC, CD and AD at the points P, Q, R and S, respectively, and ∠B = 90°. If AD = 24 cm, AB = 27 cm and DR = 6 cm, then what is the circumference of the circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Tangents from an external point are equal: DR = DS = 6 cm.

AS = AD − DS = 24 − 6 = 18 cm, and AP = AS = 18 cm.

PB = AB − AP = 27 − 18 = 9 cm.

Since angle B = 900, the radius r of the inscribed circle is equal to PB = 9 cm.

Circumference = 2 × π × r = 2 × π × 9 = 18π.

∴ The correct answer is 18π cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

∠B = 90°, AD = 24 cm, AB = 27 cm, DR = 6 cm

Circle touches AB at P, BC at Q, CD at R, and AD at S.

Formula Used:

Tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.

AP = AS, BP = BQ, CR = CQ, DR = DS

Since ∠B = 90°, the radius of the circle is equal to BP = BQ.

Calculation:

DS = DR = 6 cm

⇒ AS = AD − DS

⇒ AS = 24 − 6 = 18 cm

⇒ AP = AS = 18 cm

⇒ BP = AB − AP

⇒ BP = 27 − 18 = 9 cm

Since ∠B = 90°,

⇒ r = BP = BQ = 9 cm

⇒ Circumference = 2πr

⇒ Circumference = 2 × π × 9

⇒ Circumference = 18π cm

∴ The circumference of the circle is 18π cm.

Additional Information

Tangents from External Points

The lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are always equal (e.g., $AP = AS$).

Tangential Quadrilateral (Pitot Theorem)

For any quadrilateral circumscribed around a circle, the sum of opposite sides is equal: $AB + CD = BC + DA$.

Radius at Perpendicular Tangents

If two tangents are perpendicular to each other, the radii to the points of contact and the tangents form a square of side length $r$.

questions.question: ΔABC and ΔDBC are on the same base BC but on opposite sides of it. AD and BC intersect each other perpendicularly at O. If AO = a cm, DO = b cm and the area of ΔABC = x cm 2 , then what is the area (in cm 2 ) of ΔDBC?
questions.questionHtml: ΔABC and ΔDBC are on the same base BC but on opposite sides of it. AD and BC intersect each other perpendicularly at O. If AO = a cm, DO = b cm and the area of ΔABC = x cm<sup>2</sup>, then what is the area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of ΔDBC?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For triangles sharing the same base, the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of their heights.

Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔDBC) = Height(AO) ÷ Height(DO)

x ÷ Area(ΔDBC) = a ÷ b

Area(ΔDBC) = (b ÷ a) × x = bx/a

∴ The correct answer is bx/a cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: AO = a cm, DO = b cm, Area(ΔABC) = x cm2. AD ⊥ BC at O.

Formula Used: Area of triangle = 1/2 × base × height.

⇒ Area(ΔABC) = 1/2 × BC × AO

⇒ x = 1/2 × BC × a

⇒ BC = 2x / a

⇒ Area(ΔDBC) = 1/2 × BC × DO

⇒ Area(ΔDBC) = 1/2 × (2x / a) × b

⇒ Area(ΔDBC) = (x × b) / a

⇒ Area(ΔDBC) = bx/a

∴ The correct answer is bx/a cm2.

Additional Information

Triangle Area Ratios

If two triangles have the same base, the ratio of their areas is equal to the ratio of their altitudes: Area1/Area2 = h1/h2.

Triangles between Parallels

Two triangles having the same base and lying between the same parallel lines have equal areas.

Median Property

A median of a triangle divides it into two triangles of equal area because they share the same height and have equal bases.

questions.question: Three fractions, x, y, and z, are such that x > y > z. When the smallest of them is divided by the greatest, the result is 9/16, which exceeds y by 0.0625. If \(x + y + z = 1\frac{{13}}{{24}},\) then the value of x + z is:
questions.questionHtml: Three fractions, x, y, and z, are such that x > y > z. When the smallest of them is divided by the greatest, the result is 9/16, which exceeds y by 0.0625. If \(x + y + z = 1\frac{{13}}{{24}},\) then the value of x + z is:
questions.solution:
Given:

x > y > z

\(\frac{z}{x} = \frac{9}{16}\)

\(\frac{z}{x} = y + 0.0625\)

\(x + y + z = 1\frac{13}{24}\)

Formula used:

Basic fraction arithmetic

Calculation:

⇒ \(\frac{9}{16} = y + 0.0625\)

⇒ \(\frac{9}{16} = y + \frac{1}{16}\)

⇒ \(y = \frac{9}{16} - \frac{1}{16} = \frac{8}{16} = \frac{1}{2}\)

⇒ \(x + y + z = \frac{37}{24}\)

⇒ \(x + \frac{1}{2} + z = \frac{37}{24}\)

⇒ \(x + z = \frac{37}{24} - \frac{1}{2}\)

⇒ \(x + z = \frac{37 - 12}{24} = \frac{25}{24}\)

∴ The correct answer is option (4).

questions.question: If \(x = \frac{{\sqrt 5 - \sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 5 + \sqrt 3 }}\) and y is the reciprocal of x, then what is the value of (x 3 + y 3 )?
questions.questionHtml: If \(x = \frac{{\sqrt 5 - \sqrt 3 }}{{\sqrt 5 + \sqrt 3 }}\) and y is the reciprocal of x, then what is the value of (x3 + y3)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

If x = (√a − √b) / (√a + √b) and y = 1/x, then x + y = 2(a + b) / (a − b).

Substituting a = 5 and b = 3: x + y = 2(5 + 3) / (5 − 3) = 2 × 8 / 2 = 8.

Since y is the reciprocal of x, xy = 1.

Value of x3 + y3 = (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y) = 83 − 3(1)(8).

Final Result = 512 − 24 = 488.

∴ The correct answer is 488.

Alternate Method

Given: x = (√5 − √3) / (√5 + √3) and y = 1/x

Formula: x3 + y3 = (x + y)3 − 3xy(x + y)

⇒ Rationalizing x: x = [(√5 − √3) × (√5 − √3)] / [(√5 + √3) × (√5 − √3)]

⇒ x = (5 + 3 − 2√15) / (5 − 3) = (8 − 2√15) / 2 = 4 − √15

⇒ Similarly, y = 1/x = 4 + √15

⇒ x + y = (4 − √15) + (4 + √15) = 8

⇒ xy = (4 − √15)(4 + √15) = 16 − 15 = 1

⇒ x3 + y3 = 83 − 3 × 1 × 8

⇒ x3 + y3 = 512 − 24 = 488

∴ The correct answer is 488.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

The sum of cubes is given by a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2) or a3 + b3 = (a + b)3 − 3ab(a + b).

Rationalizing the Denominator

To rationalize a denominator like (√a + √b), multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate (√a − √b).

Reciprocal Sum Property

If x = a − √b and y = a + √b where a2 − b = 1, then x and y are reciprocals (xy = 1).

questions.question: If 8x 3 – 27y 3 = (Ax + By) (Cx 2 – Dy 2 + 6xy), then what is the value of (A + B + C – D)?
questions.questionHtml: If 8x<sup>3</sup> – 27y<sup>3</sup> = (Ax + By) (Cx<sup>2</sup> – Dy<sup>2 </sup>+ 6xy), then what is the value of (A + B + C – D)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify the identity: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2)

Here, (2x)3 − (3y)3 = (2x − 3y)(4x2 + 6xy + 9y2)

Comparing coefficients: A = 2, B = −3, C = 4, −D = 9 ⇒ D = −9

Required value: A + B + C − D = 2 − 3 + 4 − (−9) = 12

∴ The correct answer is 12.

Alternate Method

Given Equation: 8x3 − 27y3 = (Ax + By) (Cx2 − Dy2 + 6xy)

Formula Used: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2)

⇒ 8x3 − 27y3 = (2x)3 − (3y)3

⇒ (2x − 3y) ((2x)2 + (2x)(3y) + (3y)2)

⇒ (2x − 3y) (4x2 + 6xy + 9y2)

Now, comparing this with the given RHS: (Ax + By) (Cx2 − Dy2 + 6xy)

⇒ Ax + By = 2x − 3y ⇒ A = 2, B = −3

⇒ Cx2 − Dy2 + 6xy = 4x2 + 9y2 + 6xy

⇒ C = 4 and −D = 9 ⇒ D = −9

⇒ Value of (A + B + C − D) = 2 + (−3) + 4 − (−9)

⇒ 2 − 3 + 4 + 9 = 12

∴ The correct answer is 12.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

The identity for the sum of two cubes is a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2).

Whole Cube Expansion

(a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b), which is different from the difference of two cubes identity.

Coefficient Comparison

When two algebraic expressions are identical for all values of variables, the coefficients of corresponding terms (like x, y, x2, xy) must be equal.

questions.question: What is the ratio of the third proportional to 0.4 and 0.8, to the mean proportional between 13.5 and 0.24?
questions.questionHtml: What is the ratio of the third proportional to 0.4 and 0.8, to the mean proportional between 13.5 and 0.24?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Third proportional of a and b = b2 ÷ a

⇒ Third proportional (P1) = (0.8 × 0.8) ÷ 0.4 = 0.64 ÷ 0.4 = 1.6

Mean proportional of x and y = √(x × y)

⇒ Mean proportional (P2) = √(13.5 × 0.24) = √3.24 = 1.8

Required Ratio = 1.6 : 1.8 = 16 : 18 = 8 : 9

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 9.

Alternate Method

Given:

Numbers for third proportional: a = 0.4, b = 0.8

Numbers for mean proportional: x = 13.5, y = 0.24

Formula Used:

Third Proportional (c) of a and b is given by a : b = b : c ⇒ c = b2/a

Mean Proportional (m) of x and y is given by x : m = m : y ⇒ m = √(xy)

Calculations:

⇒ Let the third proportional be P1.

⇒ P1 = (0.8 × 0.8) ÷ 0.4

⇒ P1 = 0.64 ÷ 0.4 = 1.6

⇒ Let the mean proportional be P2.

⇒ P2 = √(13.5 × 0.24)

⇒ P2 = √(3.24)

⇒ P2 = 1.8

⇒ Required Ratio = P1 : P2

⇒ Required Ratio = 1.6 : 1.8

⇒ Multiply both by 10: 16 : 18

⇒ Divide both by 2: 8 : 9

∴ The correct answer is 8 : 9.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the mean proportional x satisfies a : x = x : b, giving x = √(ab).

Third Proportional

For two numbers a and b, the third proportional c satisfies a : b = b : c, giving c = b2/a.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers a, b, and c, the fourth proportional d satisfies a : b = c : d, giving d = (b × c)/a.

Continued Proportion

Three quantities a, b, c are in continued proportion if a : b = b : c, which implies b2 = ac.

questions.question: A, B and C start a business. A invests \(33\frac{1}{3}\% \) of the total capital, B invests 25% of the remaining and C invests the rest. If the total profit at the end of a year is Rs. 1,62,000 then A’s share in profit is:
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C start a business. A invests \(33\frac{1}{3}\% \) of the total capital, B invests 25% of the remaining and C invests the rest. If the total profit at the end of a year is Rs. 1,62,000 then A’s share in profit is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

A's investment is 33 1/3% (or 1/3) of the total capital.

Since the time period for all partners is the same, the profit sharing ratio is identical to the investment ratio.

A's share of profit = 33 1/3% of total profit → (1/3) × 1,62,000.

A's share = Rs. 54,000.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 54,000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Profit = Rs. 1,62,000

A's investment = 33 1/3% of total capital

B's investment = 25% of the remaining capital

Formula Used:

Profit Share = Investment × Time period

Calculations:

⇒ Let total capital = 1 unit

⇒ A's investment = 33 1/3% = 1/3

⇒ Remaining capital = 1 − 1/3 = 2/3

⇒ B's investment = 25% of 2/3 = 1/4 × 2/3 = 1/6

⇒ C's investment = 2/3 − 1/6 = (4 − 1)/6 = 3/6 = 1/2

⇒ Investment ratio A : B : C = 1/3 : 1/6 : 1/2 = 2 : 1 : 3

⇒ Total ratio parts = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 units

⇒ 6 units = Rs. 1,62,000

⇒ 1 unit = 1,62,000 ÷ 6 = Rs. 27,000

⇒ A's share (2 units) = 2 × 27,000 = Rs. 54,000

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 54,000.

Additional Information

Profit Sharing Rule

In any partnership, if the time period of investment is the same for all partners, the profit is distributed in the ratio of their capitals: P1 : P2 = C1 : C2.

Compound Partnership

If partners invest for different time periods, the profit is divided in the ratio of the product of capital and time: P1 : P2 = (C1 × T1) : (C2 × T2).

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner manages the business and may receive a salary or fixed percentage of profit before the remaining profit is distributed among all partners in their investment ratio.

questions.question: The point of intersection of the graphs of the equation 3x – 5y = 19 and 3y – 7x + 1 = 0 is P(α, β). What is the value of (3α – β)?
questions.questionHtml: The point of intersection of the graphs of the equation 3x – 5y = 19 and 3y – 7x + 1 = 0 is P(α, β). What is the value of (3α – β)?
questions.solution:
3x - 5y = 19       ----(1)

3y - 7x + 1 = 0

7x - 3y = 1       ----(2)

Subtract equation (1) from equation (2) after multiply by 3 in equation (1) and multiply by 5 in equation (2)

⇒ x = (- 2)

Put x = (- 2) in equation (1)

⇒ 3 × (- 2) - 5y = 19

⇒ - 6 - 5y = 19

⇒ - 5y = 19 + 6 = 25

⇒ y = - 25/5 = (- 5)

α = (- 2) and β = (- 5)

Now, (3α - β)

3 × (- 2) - (- 5)

⇒ (- 6) + 5

⇒ (- 1)

Therefore the correct answer is - 1.

questions.question: If x 4 – 83x 2 + 1 = 0, then a value of x 3 – x -3 can be:
questions.questionHtml: If x<sup>4</sup> – 83x<sup>2</sup> + 1 = 0, then a value of x<sup>3</sup> – x<sup>-3</sup> can be:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Divide the equation x4 − 83x2 + 1 = 0 by x2 to get x2 + 1/x2 = 83.

Find x − 1/x using the relation: x − 1/x = √(x2 + 1/x2 − 2) = √(83 − 2) = 9.

Using the cube shortcut: If x − 1/x = k, then x3 − 1/x3 = k3 + 3k.

Putting k = 9: x3 − 1/x3 = 93 + 3(9) = 729 + 27 = 756.

∴ The correct answer is 756.

Alternate Method

Given: x4 − 83x2 + 1 = 0

Formula Used: (a − b)3 = a3 − b3 − 3ab(a − b)

⇒ x4 − 83x2 + 1 = 0

⇒ (x4 + 1) / x2 = 83x2 / x2

⇒ x2 + 1/x2 = 83

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 + 2 = 83

⇒ (x − 1/x)2 = 81

⇒ x − 1/x = 9

⇒ (x − 1/x)3 = x3 − 1/x3 − 3(x)(1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ 93 = x3 − 1/x3 − 3(9)

⇒ 729 = x3 − 1/x3 − 27

⇒ x3 − 1/x3 = 729 + 27

⇒ x3 − 1/x3 = 756

∴ The correct answer is 756.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Identities for Squares

If x + 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 − 2. Conversely, if x − 1/x = k, then x2 + 1/x2 = k2 + 2.

Reciprocal Identities for Cubes

If x + 1/x = k, then x3 + 1/x3 = k3 − 3k. If x − 1/x = k, then x3 − 1/x3 = k3 + 3k.

Higher Power Reductions

Equations of the form ax4 + bx2 + a = 0 are symmetric and can be solved by dividing the entire equation by x2 to create reciprocal terms.

questions.question: If the 11-digit number 5678x43267y is divisible by 72, then the value of √(5x + 8y) is
questions.questionHtml: If the 11-digit number 5678x43267y is divisible by 72, then the value of √(5x + 8y) is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a number to be divisible by 72, it must be divisible by its coprime factors 8 and 9.

Divisibility by 8: Last three digits 67y ÷ 8 ⇒ 672 ÷ 8 = 84, so y = 2.

Divisibility by 9: Sum of digits (5+6+7+8+x+4+3+2+6+7+y) = 48 + x + y must be divisible by 9.

For y = 2, sum = 50 + x ⇒ Nearest multiple of 9 is 54, so x = 4.

Required value = √(5 × 4 + 8 × 2) = √(20 + 16) = √36 = 6.

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number: 5678x43267y

Divisibility: Divisible by 72

Formula Used:

Divisibility Rule of 8: Last three digits of the number must be divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9: Sum of all digits must be divisible by 9.

Calculations:

⇒ Divisibility by 8: Last three digits = 67y

⇒ 67y ÷ 8 ⇒ 672 ÷ 8 = 84 (Exact division)

⇒ Therefore, y = 2

⇒ Divisibility by 9: Sum of digits = 5+6+7+8+x+4+3+2+6+7+2

⇒ Sum = 50 + x

⇒ For (50 + x) to be divisible by 9, the next multiple is 54

⇒ x = 54 − 50 = 4

⇒ Value to find = √(5x + 8y)

⇒ √(5 × 4 + 8 × 2) = √(20 + 16)

⇒ √36 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Divisibility by 72

A number is divisible by 72 if and only if it is divisible by both 8 and 9, as 8 and 9 are coprime factors (HCF = 1).

Divisibility by 11

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Coprime Factor Rule

If a number N is divisible by two coprime numbers a and b, then N is also divisible by the product a × b.

questions.question: A hemispherical bowl of internal diameter 36 cm is full of a liquid. This liquid is to be filled into cylindrical bottles each of radius 3 cm and height 12 cm. How many such bottles are required to empty the bowl?
questions.questionHtml: A hemispherical bowl of internal diameter 36 cm is full of a liquid. This liquid is to be filled into cylindrical bottles each of radius 3 cm and height 12 cm. How many such bottles are required to empty the bowl?
questions.solution:
As we know,

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) × πr3

Volume of cylinder = πR2h

Radius of hemispherical bowl (r) = 36/2 = 18 cm

Radius of cylinder (R) = 3 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 12 cm

Let the number of bottles required be n then

πR2h × n = (2/3) × πr3

3 × 3 × 12 × n = (2/3) × 18 × 18 × 18

⇒ n = (2 × 18 × 18 × 18)/(3 × 3 × 3 × 12)

⇒ n = 36

So, the number of bottles required is 36.

questions.question: In a circle with centre O, AC and BD are two chords. AC and BD meet at E when produced. If AB is the diameter and ∠AEB = 68°, then the measure of ∠DOC is:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle with centre O, AC and BD are two chords. AC and BD meet at E when produced. If AB is the diameter and ∠AEB = 68°, then the measure of ∠DOC is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

AB is diameter ⇒ ∠ACB = 90° (angle in semicircle)

∠ACB is exterior angle of ▵BCE ⇒ ∠CBE = 90° − ∠AEB = 90° − 68° = 22°

∠COD = 2 × ∠CBE (central angle = 2 × inscribed angle on same arc)

∠COD = 2 × 22° = 44°

∴ The correct answer is 44°.

Alternate Method

Given:

∠AEB = 68°

Formula used:

Angle in a semicircle = 90°

Exterior angle of a triangle = Sum of the two opposite interior angles

Angle at the centre = 2 × Angle at the circumference standing on the same arc

Calculation:

AB is the diameter of the circle.

⇒ ∠ACB = 90°

∠ACB is the exterior angle of △BCE.

⇒ ∠ACB = ∠BEC + ∠CBE

⇒ 90° = 68° + ∠CBE

⇒ ∠CBE = 90° − 68°

⇒ ∠CBE = 22°

⇒ ∠COD = 2 × ∠CBE

⇒ ∠COD = 2 × 22°

⇒ ∠COD = 44°

∴ ∠COD = 44°.

Additional Information

Angle in a Semicircle

Any angle subtended by the diameter at the circumference of the circle is always 90°.

Central Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

External Intersection of Chords

If two chords AC and BD intersect at point E outside the circle, then ∠AEB = 1/2 × (major arc − minor arc).

questions.question: Let x be the least number which when divided by 15, 18, 20 and 27, the remainder in each case is 10 and x is a multiple of 31. What least number should be added to x to make it a perfect square?
questions.questionHtml: Let x be the least number which when divided by 15, 18, 20 and 27, the remainder in each case is 10 and x is a multiple of 31. What least number should be added to x to make it a perfect square?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

LCM(15, 18, 20, 27) = 540.

x = 540k + 10 must be divisible by 31.

Testing k: (13k + 10) ÷ 31 ⇒ 13(4) + 10 = 62, which is 31 × 2.

x = 540 × 4 + 10 = 2170.

Next perfect square after 2170 is 472 = 2209.

Number to be added = 2209 − 2170 = 39.

∴ The correct answer is 39.

Alternate Method

Given: Divisors are 15, 18, 20, 27 with remainder 10. x is a multiple of 31.

Step 1: Find LCM of 15, 18, 20, and 27.

⇒ 15 = 3 × 5

⇒ 18 = 2 × 32

⇒ 20 = 22 × 5

⇒ 27 = 33

⇒ LCM = 22 × 33 × 5 = 4 × 27 × 5 = 540

Step 2: Find the least multiple of 31 in the form 540k + 10.

⇒ (540k + 10) ÷ 31

⇒ (31 × 17k + 13k + 10) ÷ 31

⇒ 13k + 10 should be a multiple of 31.

⇒ For k = 4: 13 × 4 + 10 = 52 + 10 = 62 (Divisible by 31)

⇒ x = 540 × 4 + 10 = 2170

Step 3: Find the next perfect square.

⇒ √2170 ≈ 46.58

⇒ Next integer = 47

⇒ 472 = 2209

⇒ Difference = 2209 − 2170 = 39

∴ The correct answer is 39.

Additional Information

General Form of Numbers with Constant Remainder

Any number x which when divided by a, b, c leaves remainder R is given by x = LCM(a, b, c) × k + R.

Perfect Square Estimation

To find the number to be added, calculate √x, take the next integer n, and find n2 − x.

Divisibility Check for Variables

When solving (Ak + B) ÷ D, reduce A by taking A mod D to simplify the testing of k values.

questions.question: To do a certain work, the ratio of the efficiencies of X and Y is 5 ∶ 4 Working together, they can complete the same work in 10 days. Y alone starts work and leaves after 5 days. The remaining work completed by X alone in
questions.questionHtml: To do a certain work, the ratio of the efficiencies of X and Y is 5 ∶ 4 Working together, they can complete the same work in 10 days. Y alone starts work and leaves after 5 days. The remaining work completed by X alone in
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of efficiencies X : Y = 5 : 4

Total efficiency of (X + Y) = 5 + 4 = 9 units/day

Total work = Combined efficiency × Days = 9 × 10 = 90 units

Work done by Y in 5 days = 4 × 5 = 20 units

Remaining work = 90 − 20 = 70 units

Time taken by X alone = 70 ÷ 5 = 14 days

∴ The correct answer is 14 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Efficiency ratio of X to Y = 5 : 4

Time taken by X and Y together = 10 days

Time for which Y worked alone = 5 days

Formula Used:

Total Work = Total Efficiency × Total Time

Time = Work ÷ Efficiency

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
X + Y 10 90 9
X - 5
Y - 4

Calculations:

⇒ Let efficiency of X = 5 units/day and efficiency of Y = 4 units/day

⇒ Combined efficiency of X and Y = 5 + 4 = 9 units/day

⇒ Total work = 9 × 10 = 90 units

⇒ Work completed by Y in 5 days = 4 × 5 = 20 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done by Y

⇒ Remaining work = 90 − 20 = 70 units

⇒ Time taken by X to complete remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Efficiency of X

⇒ Time taken by X = 70 ÷ 5 = 14 days

∴ The correct answer is 14 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. If the efficiency ratio is a:b, the time ratio will be b:a.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person, which is Efficiency × Time.

Combined Work Formula

If A takes 'x' days and B takes 'y' days, together they take (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days to complete the work.

All the pipes were opened together at 10:30 AM, but C was closed at 2:30 PM. If the tank was full at 8:30 PM on the same day, then what is the value of x?

questions.question: If the price of petrol increases by 19% and Sunitha intends to spend only an additional 12% on petrol, by what percent should she reduce the quantity of petrol purchased (nearest to an integer)?
questions.questionHtml: If the price of petrol increases by 19% and Sunitha intends to spend only an additional 12% on petrol, by what percent should she reduce the quantity of petrol purchased (nearest to an integer)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let the initial expenditure be 100.

New Price = 100 + 19 = 119; Target Expenditure = 100 + 12 = 112.

Quantity reduction % = (New Price − Target Expenditure) ÷ New Price × 100

⇒ (119 − 112) ÷ 119 × 100 = 700 ÷ 119 ≈ 5.88%.

∴ The correct answer is 6%.

Alternate Method

Given: Price increase = 19%, Intended expenditure increase = 12%

Formula: Expenditure = Price × Quantity

⇒ Let original Price = 100 and original Quantity = 100.

⇒ Original Expenditure = 100 × 100 = 10,000.

⇒ New Price = 100 + 19 = 119.

⇒ New Expenditure = 10,000 + 12% of 10,000 = 11,200.

⇒ New Quantity = 11,200 ÷ 119 ≈ 94.117.

⇒ Percentage reduction in quantity = 100 − 94.117 = 5.883%.

⇒ Nearest integer = 6%.

∴ The correct answer is 6%.

Additional Information

Price-Consumption-Expenditure Rule

When the price of a commodity increases by P% and the expenditure increases by E%, the new consumption is (100+E)/(100+P) of the original consumption.

Constant Expenditure Case

If the expenditure remains constant (0% increase), the percentage reduction in consumption is given by [r/(100+r)] × 100, where r is the percentage increase in price.

Successive Percentage Formula

Net % change in expenditure can also be calculated as [a + b + (ab/100)]%, where a is % change in price and b is % change in consumption.

questions.question: When a two-digit number is multiplied by the sum of its digits, the product is 424. When the number obtained by interchanging its digits is multiplied by the sum of the digits, the result is 280. The sum of the digits of the given number is:
questions.questionHtml: When a two-digit number is multiplied by the sum of its digits, the product is 424. When the number obtained by interchanging its digits is multiplied by the sum of the digits, the result is 280. The sum of the digits of the given number is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 8
Key Points
  • Let the two-digit number be represented as 10x + y, where x is the tens digit and y is the units digit.
  • The sum of the digits is (x + y).
  • According to the first condition: When the number is multiplied by the sum of its digits, the product is 424.
    (10x + y)(x + y) = 424 −−− (Equation 1)
  • The number obtained by interchanging its digits is 10y + x.
  • According to the second condition: When this new number is multiplied by the sum of the digits, the result is 280.
    (10y + x)(x + y) = 280 −−− (Equation 2)
  • To find the sum of the digits, add Equation 1 and Equation 2:
    (10x + y)(x + y) + (10y + x)(x + y) = 424 + 280
    (x + y) [(10x + y) + (10y + x)] = 704
    (x + y) [11x + 11y] = 704
    (x + y) * 11(x + y) = 704
  • Simplify the equation:
    11(x + y)2 = 704
    (x + y)2 = 704 ÷ 11
    (x + y)2 = 64
  • Taking the square root of both sides:
    x + y = √64
    x + y = 8
  • The sum of the digits of the given number is 8. Therefore, Option 4 is the correct answer.
Additional Information
  • A two-digit number can always be expressed in the form 10t + u, where t is the tens place and u is the units place.
  • If we need to find the specific number in this problem:
    We know x + y = 8.
    From Equation 1: (10x + y)(8) = 424, which means 10x + y = 53.
    By comparing, the tens digit x = 5 and the units digit y = 3.
    The original number is 53, and the interchanged number is 35.
  • Check: 35 * 8 = 280, which matches the second condition given in the question.
  • The sum of digits (5 + 3) is 8.

questions.question: If \(\sqrt {10 - 2\sqrt {21} } + \sqrt {8 + 2\sqrt {15} } = \sqrt a + \sqrt b ,\) where a and b are positive integers, then the value of √(ab) is closet to:
questions.questionHtml: If \(\sqrt {10 - 2\sqrt {21} } + \sqrt {8 + 2\sqrt {15} } = \sqrt a + \sqrt b ,\) where a and b are positive integers, then the value of √(ab) is closet to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Break the surds using the rule: √(x ± 2√y) = √m ± √n where m+n=x and m×n=y.

√(10 − 2√21) = √7 − √3 (since 7+3=10 and 7×3=21)

√(8 + 2√15) = √5 + √3 (since 5+3=8 and 5×3=15)

Sum = (√7 − √3) + (√5 + √3) = √7 + √5

Comparing with √a + √b, we get a = 7 and b = 5.

√(ab) = √(7 × 5) = √35 ≈ 5.9

∴ The correct answer is 5.9.

Alternate Method

Given Expression: √(10 − 2√21) + √(8 + 2√15) = √a + √b

Step 1: Simplify √(10 − 2√21)

⇒ √(10 − 2√21) = √[7 + 3 − 2√(7 × 3)]

⇒ √[(√7)2 + (√3)2 − 2√7√3]

⇒ √[(√7 − √3)2] = √7 − √3

Step 2: Simplify √(8 + 2√15)

⇒ √(8 + 2√15) = √[5 + 3 + 2√(5 × 3)]

⇒ √[(√5)2 + (√3)2 + 2√5√3]

⇒ √[(√5 + √3)2] = √5 + √3

Step 3: Combine the simplified terms

⇒ (√7 − √3) + (√5 + √3) = √7 + √5

⇒ √a + √b = √7 + √5

⇒ a = 7, b = 5 (as a and b are positive integers)

Step 4: Calculate √(ab)

⇒ √(ab) = √(7 × 5) = √35

⇒ Since 5.92 = 34.81 and 6.02 = 36

⇒ √35 ≈ 5.916

∴ The correct answer is 5.9.

Additional Information

Square Root of a Surd

A surd of the form √(x ± 2√y) can be simplified to √m ± √n only when x = m + n and y = mn. This is based on the identity (a ± b)2 = a2 + b2 ± 2ab.

Root Approximations

Common square root values helpful in exams: √2 ≈ 1.414, √3 ≈ 1.732, √5 ≈ 2.236, √6 ≈ 2.449, √7 ≈ 2.645.

Comparing Surds

To compare √a + √b with √c + √d, if a+b = c+d, the one with the larger product ab is larger.

questions.question: Sujata marks an article 36% above the cost price and allows a 40% discount on the marked price. The loss percentage is∶
questions.questionHtml: Sujata marks an article 36% above the cost price and allows a 40% discount on the marked price. The loss percentage is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Successive percentage change formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b)/100

Here, markup percentage (a) = +36% and discount percentage (b) = −40%

Net change = 36 − 40 + (36 × −40)/100

Net change = −4 − 14.4 = −18.4%

Negative sign indicates a loss of 18.4%.

∴ The correct answer is 18.4%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup % = 36%

Discount % = 40%

Formula Used:

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

Loss % = [(CP − SP) / CP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 36% of 100 = 136

⇒ Discount = 40% of 136 = (40 ÷ 100) × 136 = 54.4

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 136 − 54.4 = 81.6

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 81.6 = 18.4

⇒ Loss Percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = (18.4 / 100) × 100 = 18.4%

∴ The correct answer is 18.4%.

Additional Information

Marked Price and Markup

Marked price is the price displayed on the product. Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100.

Successive Percentage Rule

When a value is changed by x% and then by y%, the net change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Profit and Loss Relation

Profit occurs when SP > CP, and Loss occurs when CP > SP. Both are always calculated on CP unless stated otherwise.

questions.question: Two-third of the number of employees of a company are males and the rest are females. If 3/8 of the male employees and 2/5 of the female employees are temporary employees and the total number of permanent employees is 740, then 7/15 of the total number of employees exceeds the number of temporary female employees by:
questions.questionHtml: Two-third of the number of employees of a company are males and the rest are females. questions.question: If \(x + \frac{1}{{16x}} = 3\) , then the value of \(16{x^3} + \frac{1}{{256{x^3}}}\) is∶
questions.questionHtml: If \(x + \frac{1}{{16x}} = 3\), then the value of \(16{x^3} + \frac{1}{{256{x^3}}}\) is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Multiply the given equation by 4 to get 4x + 1/(4x) = 12.

Use the standard algebraic identity: If a + 1/a = n, then a3 + 1/a3 = n3 − 3n.

Substituting n = 12, we get 64x3 + 1/64x3 = 123 − 3(12) = 1728 − 36 = 1692.

The required expression 16x3 + 1/256x3 is exactly 1/4 of (64x3 + 1/64x3).

Value = 1692 ÷ 4 = 423.

∴ The correct answer is 423.

Alternate Method

Given: x + 1/16x = 3

To find: 16x3 + 1/256x3

Formula used: (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ x + 1/16x = 3

Multiplying both sides by 4:

⇒ 4(x + 1/16x) = 4 × 3

⇒ 4x + 1/4x = 12

Now, cubing both sides of the equation:

⇒ (4x + 1/4x)3 = 123

⇒ (4x)3 + (1/4x)3 + 3 × 4x × (1/4x) × (4x + 1/4x) = 1728

⇒ 64x3 + 1/64x3 + 3 × 1 × 12 = 1728

⇒ 64x3 + 1/64x3 + 36 = 1728

⇒ 64x3 + 1/64x3 = 1728 − 36 = 1692

Dividing the entire equation by 4 to get the required form:

⇒ (64x3 + 1/64x3) ÷ 4 = 1692 ÷ 4

⇒ 16x3 + 1/256x3 = 423

∴ The correct answer is 423.

Additional Information

Square Identity

If k + 1/k = n, then k2 + 1/k2 = n2 − 2. This is derived from (k + 1/k)2 = k2 + 1/k2 + 2.

Difference Cube Identity

If k − 1/k = n, then k3 − 1/k3 = n3 + 3n. This is derived from (k − 1/k)3 = k3 − 1/k3 − 3(k − 1/k).

Higher Power Relation

To find k4 + 1/k4, square the result of k2 + 1/k2 and subtract 2, i.e., (k2 + 1/k2)2 − 2.

questions.question: What is the compound interest on a sum Rs. 7200 for \(2\frac{2}{5}\) years at 20% p.a interest compounded yearly (nearest to an integer)?
questions.questionHtml: What is the compound interest on a sum Rs. 7200 for \(2\frac{2}{5}\) years at 20% p.a interest compounded yearly (nearest to an integer)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective rate for first 2 years = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = 44%

Rate for remaining 2/5 year = 20 × (2/5) = 8%

Total effective rate = 44 + 8 + (44 × 8)/100 = 52 + 3.52 = 55.52%

Compound Interest = 7200 × 55.52% = 3997.44 ≈ Rs. 3,997

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,997.

Alternate Method

Given: Principal (P) = Rs. 7200, Rate (R) = 20% p.a., Time (n) = 2 (2/5) years

Formula: Amount = P × (1 + R/100)full years × (1 + (R × fraction)/100)

⇒ Amount (A) = 7200 × (1 + 20/100)2 × (1 + (20 × 2/5)/100)

⇒ A = 7200 × (1.2)2 × (1 + 8/100)

⇒ A = 7200 × 1.44 × 1.08

⇒ A = 10368 × 1.08 = 11197.44

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = Amount − Principal

⇒ CI = 11197.44 − 7200 = 3997.44

⇒ Nearest Integer = Rs. 3,997

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 3,997.

Additional Information

Effective Interest Rate for Fractional Years

When the time is in fraction form (T + a/b), the rate for the fractional part is calculated as R × (a/b)% and then compounded with the previous periods.

Successive Percentage Change

For two successive changes of x% and y%, the net change is (x + y + (x × y)/100)%. This is highly effective for calculating CI for 2 years.

CI vs SI for 2 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is P(R/100)2. For the 1st year, CI and SI are always equal.

questions.question: If x + y + z = 2, xy + yz + zx = -11 and xyz = -12, then what is the value of \(\sqrt {{x^3} + {y^3} + {z^3} - 2}\) ?
questions.questionHtml: If x + y + z = 2, xy + yz + zx = -11 and xyz = -12, then what is the value of \(\sqrt {{x^3} + {y^3} + {z^3} - 2}\)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct cubic identity: x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)[(x + y + z)2 − 3(xy + yz + zx)]

Substitute values: x3 + y3 + z3 − 3(−12) = 2[22 − 3(−11)]

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 + 36 = 2[4 + 33] = 2 × 37 = 74

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 = 74 − 36 = 38

⇒ Required value = √(38 − 2) = √36 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Alternate Method

Given: x + y + z = 2, xy + yz + zx = −11, xyz = −12

Formula used: (x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ 22 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(−11)

⇒ 4 = x2 + y2 + z2 − 22

⇒ x2 + y2 + z2 = 26

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 − 3xyz = (x + y + z)(x2 + y2 + z2 − (xy + yz + zx))

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 − 3(−12) = 2(26 − (−11))

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 + 36 = 2(26 + 11)

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 + 36 = 2 × 37 = 74

⇒ x3 + y3 + z3 = 38

⇒ Expression = √(x3 + y3 + z3 − 2)

⇒ Expression = √(38 − 2) = √36 = 6

∴ The correct answer is 6.

Additional Information

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

The formula a3 + b3 + c3 − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a2 + b2 + c2 − ab − bc − ca) is a fundamental identity used to solve symmetric equations.

Special Case: a + b + c = 0

If the sum of three variables is zero (a + b + c = 0), then the sum of their cubes equals three times their product: a3 + b3 + c3 = 3abc.

Square of a Trinomial

The square of a sum of three terms is given by (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2(ab + bc + ca).

questions.question: The average of 33 numbers is 74. The average of the first 17 numbers is 72.8 and that of the last 17 numbers is 77.2 If the 17 th number is excluded, then what will be the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: The average of 33 numbers is 74. The average of the first 17 numbers is 72.8 and that of the last 17 numbers is 77.2 If the 17<sup>th</sup> number is excluded, then what will be the average of the remaining numbers (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net deviation from the original average (74):

First 17 numbers: 17 × (72.8 − 74) = 17 × (−1.2) = −20.4

Last 17 numbers: 17 × (77.2 − 74) = 17 × (+3.2) = +54.4

Excess value of 17th number = −20.4 + 54.4 = 34

Average of remaining 32 numbers = 74 − (Excess ÷ Remaining Count) = 74 − (34 ÷ 32) = 74 − 1.0625 = 72.9375

∴ The correct answer is 72.9.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total numbers (n) = 33 | Average = 74

First 17 numbers average = 72.8 | Last 17 numbers average = 77.2

Formula used: Sum = Average × Number of items

⇒ Sum of all 33 numbers = 33 × 74 = 2442

⇒ Sum of first 17 numbers = 17 × 72.8 = 1237.6

⇒ Sum of last 17 numbers = 17 × 77.2 = 1312.4

⇒ Sum of (first 17 + last 17) numbers = 1237.6 + 1312.4 = 2550

⇒ 17th number = 2550 − 2442 = 108

⇒ Sum of remaining 32 numbers = 2442 − 108 = 2334

⇒ New Average = 2334 ÷ 32 = 72.9375

⇒ New Average (rounded) ≈ 72.9

∴ The correct answer is 72.9.

Additional Information

Net Deviation Method

In any group, the sum of deviations of all observations from their mean is always zero (∑(xi − xavg) = 0).

Effect of Exclusion

If a number greater than the average is excluded, the new average decreases. If a number smaller than the average is excluded, the new average increases.

New Average Formula

New Average = (Old Sum − Excluded Value) ÷ (Original Count − 1)

questions.question: A man sells his goods at a certain price at 20% profit. If the price at which he buys the goods increases by 10% and he sells them at an 8% higher price, then what will be his profit percent (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.questionHtml: A man sells his goods at a certain price at 20% profit. If the price at which he buys the goods increases by 10% and he sells them at an 8% higher price, then what will be his profit percent (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 17.8
Key Points
  • Assume the Initial Cost Price (CP) of the goods is 100 units.
  • Since the man sells the goods at a 20% profit, the Initial Selling Price (SP) is calculated as: 100 + (20% of 100) = 120 units.
  • The problem states that the New Cost Price (CP) increases by 10%. Thus, the New CP = 100 + (10% of 100) = 110 units.
  • The man then sells them at an 8% higher price than the initial selling price. The New Selling Price (SP) = 120 + (8% of 120).
  • Calculating 8% of 120: (8 ÷ 100) * 120 = 9.6. So, the New SP = 120 + 9.6 = 129.6 units.
  • The New Profit earned is the difference between the New SP and the New CP: 129.6 − 110 = 19.6 units.
  • To find the Profit Percentage, we use the formula: (Profit ÷ New CP) * 100.
  • Calculation: (19.6 ÷ 110) * 100 = 1960 ÷ 110 = 17.818...%
  • When rounded to one decimal place, the profit percent is 17.8%.
Additional Information
  • Profit is defined as the surplus amount gained when the Selling Price (SP) exceeds the Cost Price (CP). Formula: Profit = SP − CP.
  • The Profit Percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price unless specifically mentioned otherwise in the problem. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) * 100.
  • When there is a Percentage Increase in a value, the new value can be found using: New Value = Original Value * (1 + Rate ÷ 100). For an 8% increase on 120: 120 * (1 + 8 ÷ 100) = 120 * 1.08 = 129.6.

questions.question: The value of (tan29° cot61° – cosec 2 61°) + cot 2 54° – sec 2 36° + (sin 2 1° + sin 2 3° + sin 2 5° + ---------- + sin 2 89°) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of (tan29° cot61° – cosec<sup>2</sup>61°) + cot<sup>2</sup>54° – sec<sup>2</sup>36° + (sin<sup>2</sup>1° + sin<sup>2</sup>3° + sin<sup>2</sup>5° + ---------- + sin<sup>2</sup>89°) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Term 1: tan 29° cot 61° − cosec2 61° = cot2 61° − cosec2 61° = −1

Term 2: cot2 54° − sec2 36° = cot2 54° − cosec2 54° = −1

Series: sin2 1° + sin2 3° + ... + sin2 89° has n = [(89 − 1) ÷ 2] + 1 = 45 terms.

Value of series = (44 ÷ 2) + sin2 45° = 22 + 1/2 = 22.5.

Final Value = −1 − 1 + 22.5 = 20.5.

∴ The correct answer is 20 1/2.

Alternate Method

Given: (tan 29° cot 61° − cosec2 61°) + cot2 54° − sec2 36° + (sin2 1° + sin2 3° + ... + sin2 89°)

Formula Used: tan A = cot(90 − A); sec A = cosec(90 − A); sin2 A + sin2(90 − A) = 1; cot2 θ − cosec2 θ = −1

⇒ Part 1: tan 29° cot 61° − cosec2 61° = cot 61° × cot 61° − cosec2 61° = cot2 61° − cosec2 61° = −1

⇒ Part 2: cot2 54° − sec2 36° = cot2 54° − cosec2 54° = −1

⇒ Part 3 (Series): sin2 1° + sin2 3° + ... + sin2 89°

⇒ Angle AP: a = 1, d = 2, l = 89. Number of terms n = [(89 − 1) ÷ 2] + 1 = 45.

⇒ Number of complementary pairs (A + B = 90°) = 44 ÷ 2 = 22.

⇒ Sum = (22 × 1) + sin2 45° = 22 + (1/√2)2 = 22 + 1/2 = 22.5.

⇒ Total = (−1) + (−1) + 22.5 = 20.5.

∴ The correct answer is 20 1/2.

Additional Information

Complementary Trigonometric Ratios

When A + B = 90°, sin2 A + sin2 B = 1 and cos2 A + cos2 B = 1. Also, tan A = cot B and sec A = cosec B.

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

sin2 θ + cos2 θ = 1; 1 + tan2 θ = sec2 θ; 1 + cot2 θ = cosec2 θ.

Terms in a Series

For an arithmetic progression, the number of terms n = [(Last term − First term) ÷ Common difference] + 1.

questions.question: The graphs of the equations 2x + 3y = 11 and x – 2y + 12 = 0 intersects at P(x 1 , y 1 ) and the graph of the equation x – 2y + 12 = 0 intersects the x-axis at Q(x 2 , y 2 ). What is the value of (x 1 – x 2 + y 1 + y 2 )?
questions.questionHtml: The graphs of the equations 2x + 3y = 11 and x – 2y + 12 = 0 intersects at P(x<sub>1</sub>, y<sub>1</sub>) and the graph of the equation x – 2y + 12 = 0 intersects the x-axis at Q(x<sub>2</sub>, y<sub>2</sub>). What is the value of (x<sub>1</sub> – x<sub>2</sub> + y<sub>1</sub> + y<sub>2</sub>)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Solve 2x + 3y = 11 and x − 2y = −12 simultaneously by multiplying second equation by 2: 2x − 4y = −24.

Subtracting both: (2x + 3y) − (2x − 4y) = 11 − (−24) ⇒ 7y = 35 ⇒ y1 = 5 and x1 = −2.

For point Q on x-axis in x − 2y + 12 = 0, put y = 0 ⇒ x2 = −12 and y2 = 0.

Required value = x1 − x2 + y1 + y2 = −2 − (−12) + 5 + 0 = 15.

∴ The correct answer is 15.

Alternate Method

Given:

Line 1: 2x + 3y = 11

Line 2: x − 2y + 12 = 0

P(x1, y1) is the intersection of Line 1 and Line 2.

Q(x2, y2) is the intersection of Line 2 and the x-axis.

Step 1: Finding coordinates of P(x1, y1)

Multiply x − 2y = −12 by 2:

⇒ 2x − 4y = −24 --- (i)

Given first equation:

⇒ 2x + 3y = 11 --- (ii)

Subtract (i) from (ii):

⇒ (2x + 3y) − (2x − 4y) = 11 − (−24)

⇒ 7y = 35 ⇒ y1 = 5

Substitute y = 5 in Line 2:

⇒ x − 2(5) + 12 = 0

⇒ x − 10 + 12 = 0 ⇒ x1 = −2

⇒ P(x1, y1) = (−2, 5)

Step 2: Finding coordinates of Q(x2, y2)

Since Q lies on the x-axis, y-coordinate y2 = 0.

Substitute y = 0 in equation of Line 2: x − 2y + 12 = 0

⇒ x − 2(0) + 12 = 0

⇒ x + 12 = 0 ⇒ x2 = −12

⇒ Q(x2, y2) = (−12, 0)

Step 3: Calculating the required value

⇒ (x1 − x2 + y1 + y2)

⇒ (−2 − (−12) + 5 + 0)

⇒ −2 + 12 + 5 + 0 = 15

∴ The correct answer is 15.

Additional Information

Intersection of Two Lines

The point of intersection of two linear equations a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 is found by solving them simultaneously as a system of equations.

Intercepts on Axes

To find the x-intercept of a line, set y = 0. To find the y-intercept, set x = 0. A point on the x-axis always has the form (x, 0).

Condition for Parallel Lines

Two lines a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 are parallel if their slopes are equal, i.e., a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2.

questions.question: Places A and B are 396 km apart. Train X leaves from A for B and train Y leaves from B for A at the same time on the same day on parallel tracks. Both trains meet after \(5\frac{1}{2}\) hours. The speed of Y is 10 km/h more than that of X. What is the speed (in km/h) of Y?
questions.questionHtml: Places A and B are 396 km apart. Train X leaves from A for B and train Y leaves from B for A at the same time on the same day on parallel tracks. Both trains meet after \(5\frac{1}{2}\) hours. The speed of Y is 10 km/h more than that of X. What is the speed (in km/h) of Y?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed of trains = Distance ÷ Time = 396 ÷ 5.5 = 72 km/h.

Since trains move towards each other, Sum of speeds (Y + X) = 72 km/h.

Given Difference of speeds (Y − X) = 10 km/h.

Speed of faster train (Y) = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (72 + 10) ÷ 2 = 41 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 41 km/h.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance (D) = 396 km

Time (t) = 5.5 hours

Speed of train Y = Speed of train X + 10 km/h

Formula:

Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ Time taken to meet

⇒ Let speed of Train X be S km/h.

⇒ Speed of Train Y = (S + 10) km/h.

⇒ Relative Speed = S + (S + 10) = 2S + 10 km/h.

⇒ 2S + 10 = 396 ÷ 5.5

⇒ 2S + 10 = 72

⇒ 2S = 72 − 10 = 62

⇒ S = 31 km/h (Speed of Train X)

⇒ Speed of Train Y = 31 + 10 = 41 km/h.

∴ The correct answer is 41 km/h.

Additional Information

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds (S1 − S2).

Distance Formula

Distance = Relative Speed × Time. In meeting point problems, the time taken by both to meet is the same if they start simultaneously.

questions.question: Train A which was travelling at 50 km/h crosses train B travelling in opposite direction in 15 seconds. If the length of train B is three times the length of A and the speed of train B was 58 km/h, then the length of train A(in m) is∶
questions.questionHtml: Train A which was travelling at 50 km/h crosses train B travelling in opposite direction in 15 seconds. If the length of train B is three times the length of A and the speed of train B was 58 km/h, then the length of train A(in m) is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Relative speed in opposite direction = 50 + 58 = 108 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

Total distance (LA + LB) = Speed × Time = 30 × 15 = 450 m

Given LB = 3LA, so total length = LA + 3LA = 4LA

4LA = 450 ⇒ LA = 450 ÷ 4 = 112.5 m

∴ The correct answer is 112.5 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Train A (SA) = 50 km/h

Speed of Train B (SB) = 58 km/h

Time to cross each other (t) = 15 seconds

Length of Train B (LB) = 3 × Length of Train A (LA)

Formula Used:

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = SA + SB

Total Distance = Length of Train A + Length of Train B

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculations:

⇒ Relative speed = 50 + 58 = 108 km/h

⇒ Converting speed to m/s: 108 × (5/18) = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s

⇒ Total distance = (LA + LB)

⇒ LA + 3LA = 30 × 15

⇒ 4LA = 450

⇒ LA = 450 ÷ 4

⇒ LA = 112.5 m

∴ The correct answer is 112.5 m.

Additional Information

Relative Speed Rules

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2. When they move in the same direction, relative speed = |S1 − S2|.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Length

When a train crosses another train, the total distance covered is always the sum of the lengths of both trains, regardless of the direction.

questions.question: The value of tan 2 ϕ + cot 2 ϕ – sec 2 ϕ cosec 2 ϕ is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The value of tan<sup>2</sup>ϕ + cot<sup>2</sup>ϕ – sec<sup>2</sup>ϕ cosec<sup>2</sup>ϕ is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put φ = 45° to evaluate the expression quickly.

tan 45° = 1, cot 45° = 1, sec 45° = √2, cosec 45° = √2

Expression = (1)2 + (1)2 − (√2)2 × (√2)2

Expression = 1 + 1 − 2 × 2 = 2 − 4 = −2

∴ The correct answer is -2.

Alternate Method

Given: tan2φ + cot2φ − sec2φ cosec2φ

Formula Used:

1. sec2φ = 1 + tan2φ

2. cosec2φ = 1 + cot2φ

3. sec2φ cosec2φ = sec2φ + cosec2φ

Calculations:

⇒ We know that sec2φ cosec2φ = (1/cos2φ) × (1/sin2φ)

⇒ sec2φ cosec2φ = (sin2φ + cos2φ) / (sin2φ cos2φ)

⇒ sec2φ cosec2φ = (sin2φ / sin2φ cos2φ) + (cos2φ / sin2φ cos2φ)

⇒ sec2φ cosec2φ = (1 / cos2φ) + (1 / sin2φ) = sec2φ + cosec2φ

⇒ Substitute this in the original expression: tan2φ + cot2φ − (sec2φ + cosec2φ)

⇒ Using identities sec2φ = 1 + tan2φ and cosec2φ = 1 + cot2φ:

⇒ tan2φ + cot2φ − (1 + tan2φ + 1 + cot2φ)

⇒ tan2φ + cot2φ − (2 + tan2φ + cot2φ)

⇒ tan2φ + cot2φ − 2 − tan2φ − cot2φ = −2

∴ The correct answer is -2.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Identities

Standard Pythagorean identities: sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, sec2θ − tan2θ = 1, and cosec2θ − cot2θ = 1.

Product to Sum Property

For secant and cosecant: sec2θ × cosec2θ = sec2θ + cosec2θ. Similarly for tan and cot: tan2θ × cot2θ = 1.

Complementary Angles

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

questions.question: A can do 40% of a work in 12 days, whereas B can do 60% of the same work in 15 days. Both works together for 10 days. C completes the remaining work alone in 4 days. A, B and C together will complete 28% of the same work in∶
questions.questionHtml: A can do 40% of a work in 12 days, whereas B can do 60% of the same work in 15 days. Both works together for 10 days. C completes the remaining work alone in 4 days. A, B and C together will complete 28% of the same work in∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total time: A = 12 ÷ 0.4 = 30 days, B = 15 ÷ 0.6 = 25 days.

Let Total Work = LCM(30, 25) = 150 units. Efficiencies: A = 5, B = 6.

(A+B) in 10 days = (5 + 6) × 10 = 110. Rem. work = 150 − 110 = 40.

C's Efficiency = 40 ÷ 4 = 10. Total Efficiency (A+B+C) = 5 + 6 + 10 = 21.

Time for 28% work = (150 × 0.28) ÷ 21 = 42 ÷ 21 = 2 days.

∴ The correct answer is 2 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

A completes 40% in 12 days ⇒ 100% in (12 × 100) ÷ 40 = 30 days.

B completes 60% in 15 days ⇒ 100% in (15 × 100) ÷ 60 = 25 days.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 30 150 5
B 25 6

⇒ Work done by A and B in 10 days = (5 + 6) × 10 = 110 units.

⇒ Remaining work left for C = 150 − 110 = 40 units.

⇒ Efficiency of C = Remaining Work ÷ Days = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Combined efficiency of A, B and C = 5 + 6 + 10 = 21 units/day.

⇒ 28% of total work = 150 × (28 ÷ 100) = 42 units.

⇒ Time taken by A, B and C = 42 ÷ 21 = 2 days.

∴ The correct answer is 2 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relation

The time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to the efficiency. Work = Efficiency × Time.

Combined Efficiency

When multiple people work together, their combined efficiency is the sum of their individual efficiencies (Total Efficiency = E1 + E2 + ...).

Percentage Work calculation

To find the time for a partial work, multiply the total work by the percentage fraction (e.g., 28% = 28/100) before dividing by efficiency.

questions.question: The expression \(\sqrt {10 + 2\left( {\sqrt 6 - \sqrt {10} - \sqrt {15} } \right)}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The expression \(\sqrt {10 + 2\left( {\sqrt 6 - \sqrt {10} - \sqrt {15} } \right)}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The expression is in the form √[a + b + c + 2(√ab + √bc + √ca)], which is √(a + b + c)2.

Compare the signs of the products: 2(√6 − √10 − √15).

Positive term √6 comes from √2 × √3. Negative terms −√10 and −√15 share −√5 as a common factor.

Thus, the terms are √3, √2, and −√5.

Sum of squares = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10, which matches the constant term.

∴ The correct answer is √3 + √2 − √5.

Alternate Method

Given: √[10 + 2(√6 − √10 − √15)]

Formula Used: (x + y + z)2 = x2 + y2 + z2 + 2(xy + yz + zx)

Let x = √3, y = √2, and z = −√5.

⇒ x2 + y2 + z2 = (√3)2 + (√2)2 + (−√5)2 = 3 + 2 + 5 = 10

⇒ 2(xy + yz + zx) = 2[(√3 × √2) + (√2 × −√5) + (−√5 × √3)]

⇒ 2(xy + yz + zx) = 2(√6 − √10 − √15)

Substituting these into the given expression:

⇒ √[10 + 2(√6 − √10 − √15)] = √[(√3 + √2 − √5)2]

⇒ √3 + √2 − √5

∴ The correct answer is √3 + √2 − √5.

Additional Information

Square of a Trinomial

The formula (a + b + c)2 = a2 + b2 + c2 + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca helps in simplifying nested radicals with three irrational terms.

Simplification rule for Surds

When simplifying √(x ± 2√y), look for two numbers whose sum is x and product is y, then the result is √a ± √b.

BODMAS Rule

Always solve terms inside the innermost brackets first, followed by orders (roots/powers), then division, multiplication, addition, and subtraction.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 56 cm, 90 cm and 106 cm. The circumference of its circumcircle is∶
questions.questionHtml: The sides of a triangle are 56 cm, 90 cm and 106 cm. The circumference of its circumcircle is∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Check for Pythagorean triplet: 562 + 902 = 3136 + 8100 = 11236 = 1062.

Since the triangle is right-angled, the circumradius R = Hypotenuse ÷ 2 = 106 ÷ 2 = 53 cm.

Circumference of circumcircle = 2 × π × R = 2 × π × 53 = 106π cm.

∴ The correct answer is 106π cm.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sides of the triangle: a = 56 cm, b = 90 cm, c = 106 cm.

Formula Used:

For a right-angled triangle, the circumradius (R) = Hypotenuse ÷ 2.

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × R

Calculations:

⇒ First, we check if the triangle is right-angled using Pythagoras theorem:

⇒ a2 + b2 = 562 + 902 = 3136 + 8100 = 11236

⇒ c2 = 1062 = 11236

⇒ Since a2 + b2 = c2, the triangle is right-angled at the vertex opposite to the 106 cm side.

⇒ In a right-angled triangle, the circumcircle passes through all vertices, and the hypotenuse is the diameter.

⇒ Diameter (d) = Hypotenuse = 106 cm

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 106 ÷ 2 = 53 cm

⇒ Circumference = 2 × π × R = π × d

⇒ Circumference = 106π cm

∴ The correct answer is 106π cm.

Additional Information

Circumradius of any Triangle

For any triangle with sides a, b, c and area A, the circumradius R = (a × b × c) ÷ (4 × A).

Inradius of a Right-angled Triangle

The inradius (r) of a right-angled triangle is given by r = (Perpendicular + Base − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), (20, 21, 29), and (28, 45, 53).

questions.question: The number of factors of 3600 is:
questions.questionHtml: The number of factors of 3600 is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Prime factorize 3600: 3600 = 24 × 32 × 52.

For N = pa × qb × rc, Total Factors = (a+1)(b+1)(c+1).

Number of factors = (4+1) × (2+1) × (2+1) = 5 × 3 × 3 = 45.

∴ The correct answer is 45.

Alternate Method

Given Number: 3600

Formula: If a number N = p1a × p2b × p3c..., the total number of factors = (a+1) × (b+1) × (c+1)...

⇒ 3600 = 36 × 100

⇒ 3600 = (22 × 32) × (22 × 52)

⇒ 3600 = 22+2 × 32 × 52

⇒ 3600 = 24 × 32 × 52

⇒ Exponents: a = 4, b = 2, c = 2

⇒ Total Factors = (4 + 1) × (2 + 1) × (2 + 1)

⇒ Total Factors = 5 × 3 × 3 = 45

∴ The correct answer is 45.

Additional Information

Sum of Factors

The sum of all factors is calculated as Σ = [ (pa+1 − 1)/(p − 1) ] × [ (qb+1 − 1)/(q − 1) ] × ...

Product of Factors

The product of all factors of a number N is given by N(Total Factors / 2).

Even and Odd Factors

For N = 2a × qb × rc, Odd factors = (b+1)(c+1) and Even factors = a × (b+1)(c+1).

Perfect Square Factors

The number of factors that are perfect squares is calculated as ([a/2]+1) × ([b/2]+1) × ...

questions.question: If \(\frac{{1\; + \;\sin \phi }}{{1 - \sin \phi }} = \frac{{{p^2}}}{{{q^2}}}\) , then sec ϕ is equal to∶
questions.questionHtml: If \(\frac{{1\; + \;\sin \phi }}{{1 - \sin \phi }} = \frac{{{p^2}}}{{{q^2}}}\), then sec ϕ is equal to∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply Componendo and Dividendo to (1 + sin ϕ) / (1 − sin ϕ) = p2 / q2.

1 / sin ϕ = (p2 + q2) / (p2 − q2) ⇒ sin ϕ = (p2 − q2) / (p2 + q2).

Recognize the Pythagorean triplet: Perpendicular = p2 − q2, Hypotenuse = p2 + q2, Base = 2pq.

sec ϕ = Hypotenuse / Base = (p2 + q2) / 2pq.

Splitting the terms: sec ϕ = p2/2pq + q2/2pq = 1/2 (p/q + q/p).

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 (p/q + q/p).

Alternate Method

Given: (1 + sin ϕ) / (1 − sin ϕ) = p2 / q2

Formula Used: Componendo and Dividendo: If a/b = c/d, then (a + b) / (a − b) = (c + d) / (c − d). Also, sec ϕ = 1 / cos ϕ.

⇒ Applying Componendo and Dividendo:

⇒ [(1 + sin ϕ) + (1 − sin ϕ)] / [(1 + sin ϕ) − (1 − sin ϕ)] = (p2 + q2) / (p2 − q2)

⇒ 2 / 2sin ϕ = (p2 + q2) / (p2 − q2)

⇒ 1 / sin ϕ = (p2 + q2) / (p2 − q2) ⇒ sin ϕ = (p2 − q2) / (p2 + q2)

⇒ Since sin ϕ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse, we have P = p2 − q2 and H = p2 + q2.

⇒ Base (B) = √[H2 − P2] = √[(p2 + q2)2 − (p2 − q2)2]

⇒ B = √[4p2q2] = 2pq

⇒ sec ϕ = Hypotenuse / Base = (p2 + q2) / 2pq

⇒ sec ϕ = p2 / 2pq + q2 / 2pq = p/2q + q/2p = 1/2 (p/q + q/p)

∴ The correct answer is 1/2 (p/q + q/p).

Additional Information

Componendo and Dividendo Rule

It is a theorem on proportions that allows for the simplification of equations of the form (a+b)/(a−b) = k.

Pythagorean Triplet for Algebra

The set of values (p2 − q2), 2pq, and (p2 + q2) always forms a right-angled triangle triplet.

Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios

The secant function (sec ϕ) is the reciprocal of the cosine function (cos ϕ = Base/Hypotenuse), so sec ϕ = Hypotenuse/Base.

questions.question: In ΔABC, the medians AD, BE and CF meet at O. What is the ratio of the area of ΔABD to the area of ΔAOE?
questions.questionHtml: In ΔABC, the medians AD, BE and CF meet at O. What is the ratio of the area of ΔABD to the area of ΔAOE?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The three medians of a triangle divide it into 6 smaller triangles of equal area.

Area of ΔAOE = 1 part (since it is one of the 6 small triangles).

Area of ΔABD = 3 parts (since the median AD divides the triangle into two equal halves, i.e., 6/2 = 3 parts).

Ratio = Area of ΔABD : Area of ΔAOE = 3 : 1.

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.

Alternate Method

Given: In ΔABC, AD, BE, and CF are medians intersecting at centroid O.

Formula: A median divides a triangle into two triangles of equal area. The centroid divides a triangle into six triangles of equal area.

Let the total area of ΔABC be 6 units.

⇒ Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × Area of ΔABC (Property of median AD)

⇒ Area of ΔABD = 1/2 × 6 = 3 units.

⇒ The six triangles ΔAOF, ΔBOF, ΔBOD, ΔCOD, ΔCOE, and ΔAOE have equal area.

⇒ Area of ΔAOE = 1/6 × Area of ΔABC

⇒ Area of ΔAOE = 1/6 × 6 = 1 unit.

⇒ Ratio = Area(ΔABD) / Area(ΔAOE)

⇒ Ratio = 3 / 1

⇒ Ratio = 3 : 1.

∴ The correct answer is 3 : 1.

Additional Information

Centroid Property

The centroid (O) divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1. For example, AO : OD = 2 : 1, BO : OE = 2 : 1, and CO : OF = 2 : 1.

Area of Median Triangles

Area of ΔAOB = Area of ΔBOC = Area of ΔCOA = 1/3 × Area of ΔABC.

Apollonius Theorem

In ΔABC with median AD, the theorem states: AB2 + AC2 = 2(AD2 + BD2).

questions.question: If 60% of a number is 120 more than 20% of the number, then 28% of the number is less than \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the number by∶
questions.questionHtml: If 60% of a number is 120 more than 20% of the number, then 28% of the number is less than \(33\frac{1}{3}\%\) of the number by∶
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Difference in given percentages: 60% − 20% = 40%

Value of 40% = 120 ⇒ 1% = 120 ÷ 40 = 3

Required gap: 331/3% − 28% = 51/3%

Target Value = 3 × 51/3 = 3 × (16/3) = 16

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Alternate Method

Given: Difference between 60% and 20% of a number is 120.

Formula Used: Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Number

⇒ Let the number be x.

⇒ (60/100) × x − (20/100) × x = 120

⇒ (40/100) × x = 120

⇒ x = (120 × 100) ÷ 40 = 300

⇒ 331/3% of 300 = (1/3) × 300 = 100

⇒ 28% of 300 = (28/100) × 300 = 84

⇒ Difference = 100 − 84 = 16

∴ The correct answer is 16.

Additional Information

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

Standard fractions simplify calculations: 1/3 = 331/3%, 1/4 = 25%, 1/5 = 20%.

Percentage Base Rule

When the base number is the same, percentage differences can be added or subtracted directly before calculating the final value.

Percentage Change Formula

% Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

questions.question: The value of \(\frac{{\sin \left( {78^\circ + \theta } \right) - \cos \left( {12^\circ - \theta } \right) + \left( {{{\tan }^2}70^\circ - cose{c^2}20^\circ } \right)}}{{\sin 25^\circ cos65^\circ + \cos 25^\circ \sin 65^\circ }}\) is:
questions.questionHtml: The value of \(\frac{{\sin \left( {78^\circ + \theta } \right) - \cos \left( {12^\circ - \theta } \right) + \left( {{{\tan }^2}70^\circ - cose{c^2}20^\circ } \right)}}{{\sin 25^\circ cos65^\circ + \cos 25^\circ \sin 65^\circ }}\) is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Identify complementary angles: Since (78° + θ) + (12° − θ) = 90°, then sin(78° + θ) = cos(12° − θ), making their difference 0.

Simplify numerator identity: tan270° − cosec220° = tan270° − sec270° = −1 (as sec2A − tan2A = 1).

Simplify denominator: sin 25° cos 65° + cos 25° sin 65° = sin(25° + 65°) = sin 90° = 1.

Final calculation: (0 + (−1)) ÷ 1 = −1.

∴ The correct answer is −1.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression = (sin(78° + θ) − cos(12° − θ) + (tan270° − cosec220°)) ÷ (sin 25° cos 65° + cos 25° sin 65°)

Formula Used:

1. sin A = cos(90° − A)

2. sec2A − tan2A = 1 ⇒ tan2A − sec2A = −1

3. sin A cos B + cos A sin B = sin(A + B)

Calculations:

⇒ Numerator Term 1: sin(78° + θ) − cos(12° − θ)

⇒ sin(78° + θ) = cos(90° − (78° + θ)) = cos(12° − θ)

⇒ cos(12° − θ) − cos(12° − θ) = 0

⇒ Numerator Term 2: tan270° − cosec220°

⇒ cosec 20° = sec(90° − 20°) = sec 70°

⇒ tan270° − sec270° = −(sec270° − tan270°) = −1

⇒ Denominator: sin 25° cos 65° + cos 25° sin 65°

⇒ sin(25° + 65°) = sin 90° = 1

⇒ Final Value = (0 − 1) ÷ 1 = −1

∴ The correct answer is −1.

Additional Information

Complementary Angle Ratios

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Trigonometric Identities

Fundamental identities include sin2θ + cos2θ = 1, 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ, and 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

Compound Angle Formulas

sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B and cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B.
